For query tasks, prefer one short read-only command; as soon as shell output contains the exact answer, call answer_action immediately.
For state-change tasks, prefer one minimal change and then one short verification command.

Your answers should be exact and precise (for example, a single number), do not answer with full sentences or phrases.
Always use a tool provided instead of simply responding with content.

Now, I will start a new problem in a new OS. My problem is:

2. Recursively enumerate all entries under /working and save the raw listing to "temp_checks/raw_listing.txt".

4. For each path listed in "temp_checks/candidates.txt", verify its file type and write those confirmed to be regular files into "temp_checks/regular_candidates.txt".
5. Normalize and deduplicate the entries in "temp_checks/regular_candidates.txt" and save the unique canonical paths to "temp_checks/regular_unique.txt".
6. Compare the counts and contents between "temp_checks/candidates.txt" and "temp_checks/regular_unique.txt" and log any discrepancies to "temp_checks/consistency.log".
7. Create a one-line summary file "temp_checks/result_prepare.txt" containing "found" if "temp_checks/regular_unique.txt" is non-empty or "not_found" if it is empty, leaving the final yes/no decision to be made from that summary.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

{"script":"set -eu
mkdir -p temp_checks
{
  date
  uname -a || true
  id || true
  pwd
  echo "ENV:"
  env || true
  echo "ls -la /working:"
  ls -la /working 2>/dev/null || true
} > temp_checks/state.log

# raw listing
find /working -print 2>/dev/null > temp_checks/raw_listing.txt || true

# candidates: final component exactly "workspace"
grep '/workspace$' temp_checks/raw_listing.txt > temp_checks/candidates.txt || true

# verify regular files
: > temp_checks/regular_candidates.txt
while IFS= read -r p; do
  [ -f "$p" ] && printf '%s\n' "$p"
done < temp_checks/candidates.txt > temp_checks/regular_candidates.txt || true

# normalize and deduplicate
if [ -s temp_checks/regular_candidates.txt ]; then
  while IFS= read -r p; do readlink -f -- "$p" || printf '%s\n' "$p"; done < temp_checks/regular_candidates.txt | sort -u > temp_checks/regular_unique.txt
else
  : > temp_checks/regular_unique.txt
fi

# canonicalize candidates for comparison
while IFS= read -r p; do readlink -f -- "$p" || printf '%s\n' "$p"; done < temp_checks/candidates.txt | sort -u > temp_checks/candidates_canonical.txt || true

# compare and log discrepancies
c1=$(wc -l < temp_checks/candidates.txt 2>/dev/null || true)
c2=$(wc -l < temp_checks/regular_unique.txt 2>/dev/null || true)
{
  echo "candidates_count: $c1"
  echo "regular_unique_count: $c2"
  echo "only_in_candidates:"
  comm -23 <(sort -u temp_checks/candidates_canonical.txt) <(sort -u temp_checks/regular_unique.txt) || true
  echo "only_in_regular_unique:"
  comm -13 <(sort -u temp_checks/candidates_canonical.txt) <(sort -u temp_checks/regular_unique.txt) || true
} > temp_checks/consistency.log

# summary
if [ -s temp_checks/regular_unique.txt ]; then
  echo found > temp_checks/result_prepare.txt
  echo yes
else
  echo not_found > temp_checks/result_prepare.txt
  echo no
fi
"}
